subject.title: fix(cron): cap trigger script tool access

question: How should an upgrade handle existing trigger-script cron jobs whose creator-derived tool cap was never recorded and cannot be reconstructed?
rationale: The code cannot distinguish legitimate unrestricted operator jobs from jobs created through a restricted agent, so either preserving or stopping them changes a shipped security/compatibility boundary.

options.title: Quarantine Legacy Triggers
options.body: Disable trigger evaluation for cap-less legacy jobs until an operator explicitly reviews and re-saves each job with an approved tool policy.

options.title: Accept Forward-Only Hardening
options.body: Merge the branch as written and explicitly accept that existing cap-less jobs remain unrestricted until operators audit or edit them.

options.title: Design Provenance First
options.body: Hold the PR until a broader migration or provenance mechanism can classify legacy jobs without stopping all cap-less operator jobs.

recommendation.title: Quarantine Legacy Triggers
recommendation.body: Disable trigger evaluation for cap-less legacy jobs until an operator explicitly reviews and re-saves each job with an approved tool policy.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent authorization and cron-runtime history most directly spans the security and compatibility surfaces requiring a decision.
